"The Junagadh rock inscription of the Shaka ruler Rudradaman (second century CE) records the history of the Sudarshana lake: 'The lake, with well-joined water-gates and conduits... was originally built by the Vaishya Pushyagupta, the provincial governor of the Maurya King Chandragupta; a conduit was ordered to be made by the Yavanaraja Tushaspha for the Maurya King Ashoka... but in a terrible storm, the dams burst and a breach of 420 cubits occurred, emptying the lake. Rudradaman repaired the breach, making the embankment three times stronger, entirely out of his own private treasury, without oppressing the people of his country by exacting forced labour (vishti) or imposing taxes.' Later, the Gupta emperor Skandagupta also had the lake repaired in the 5th century CE."

Who originally constructed the Sudarshana lake reservoir during the reign of Chandragupta Maurya?
